text1: The Rasho-pattern escort corvette is a light support vessel, built to shepherd larger Covenant warships rather than duel alone. Its single synergy mount and generous energy shielding let it screen a flank or cover a withdrawal, while a short-range slipspace drive lets it flicker across the battle to wherever it is needed. Lightly armed for its class, it relies on the fleet it escorts; isolated and swarmed, it has little answer.

The Ceudar-pattern heavy corvette is the Covenant's frontline gunboat, a compact hull that trades range for a heavy forward punch. A hardpoint-mounted main gun and two flanking emitters let it press an engagement hard behind its energy shield, and a plasma barrage system lets it dump a burst of fire to break a target's guard. Deadly in a straight fight, it is undone the moment nimbler ships get onto its flanks.

The Ardo'nikapoora-pattern landing corvette is a troop and materiel transport, its hull given over to holds and boarding craft rather than weapons. A single point-defense emitter and a strong energy shield are its only protection, and a slipspace drive lets it slip away from a losing fight. It is not built to trade fire; caught without an escort, it survives only by running.

The SDV-class heavy corvette is the Covenant's dedicated screen, a destroyer-weight hull bristling with point-defense emitters and layered energy shielding. It exists to smother incoming missiles and strike craft around a battle group, freeing the line ships to fire unhindered. Its own guns are defensive by design; left to fight alone it can hold, but it cannot press, and a determined swarm will eventually saturate its arcs.

The CPV-class escort carrier trades the destroyer's guns for a pair of launch bays, projecting Covenant strike craft from behind a heavy shield. Slow and thinly armed, it hangs at the rear of an engagement and lets its wings do the fighting, using a short slipspace drive to reposition or disengage. Cornered without its screen, it is little more than a slow, valuable target.

The CRS-class strike destroyer is a fast, aggressive hull built to close and overwhelm. Twin forward emitters and a plasma barrage system let it dump a devastating alpha into a single target before its shield buckles, and it is quick enough to pick its fights. Fragile for its weight, it lives or dies on the opening exchange; drawn into a grind against numbers, it loses.

The Ket-pattern assault destroyer is a long-range energy platform, its broad hull built around a single heavy spinal projector. Vast flux reserves and a high-energy focus let it land punishing aimed shots from beyond most return fire, and its energy shield lets it stand its ground while it works. Slow to turn and reliant on that one great gun, it is dangerous at range and vulnerable to anything fast enough to get inside its arc.

The CCS-class battlecruiser is the backbone of a Covenant battle group and its usual command hull. A heavy spinal projector flanked by turreted emitters lets it dictate an engagement from the front, and its powerful energy shield lets it hold the line while lighter ships maneuver. Versatile and well-rounded rather than specialized, it is formidable head-on but can be pulled apart if allowed to be flanked and swarmed.

The DDS-class escort carrier is a fast fleet carrier, fielding three wings of Covenant strike craft from behind a strong shield. It carries only enough weaponry to fend off attackers while its fighters do the real work, and a targeting-feed array sharpens both its own guns and its wings. Kept at range behind an escort it is a potent force multiplier; run down and boarded, it has little to offer in a straight fight.

The ORS-class light cruiser is a fast, hard-hitting hull built to strike and reposition. A heavy forward projector and paired emitters deliver a brutal frontal salvo, and a plasma burn lets it dash into or out of range at will. Lightly built for a cruiser, it depends on speed and its shield to survive; caught flat-footed by numbers, it burns down quickly.

The RCS-class armored cruiser is a bulwark, trading firepower for sheer endurance. Heavily armored and wrapped in a deep energy shield, with a damper field to blunt incoming fire, it is built to anchor a battle line and refuse to break. Its guns are fewer and more measured than its tonnage suggests, so it grinds down opponents slowly rather than deleting them; its danger is that it simply will not die.

The ORS-class heavy cruiser is a Covenant capital ship in all but name, a battle-line dreadnought fielding a spinal projector and a broadside of heavy emitters. A displacement drive lets a hull this size reposition with alarming speed, and its shield is deep enough to trade blows with anything short of a supercapital. Rare and jealously guarded, a single ORS can be the deciding weight in a fleet action.

The CPV-class heavy destroyer is a fast, wide-hulled assault capital built to run down and shatter smaller warships. Twin forward projectors and flanking emitters deliver a heavy frontal weight of fire, and a plasma burn gives it a closing speed no ship its size should have. It carries less armor than the battle-line hulls, betting instead on speed, shield, and shock; kept at range by disciplined fire, it loses the edge that makes it dangerous.

A battleship known only from fragmentary records, the Reverence-class is the immovable heart of a Covenant battle line. Enormous armor and the deepest energy shielding of any Covenant hull let it soak punishment that would gut a lesser ship, buying time for its heavy projectors to grind the enemy down. It is slow and ponderous, and asks its escorts to keep the swarms off it; given that, it simply does not fall.

The CAS-class assault carrier is a Covenant flagship, a vessel a full tier above the battle-line and built to break fleets by itself. Its forward hemisphere is a wall of heavy projectors behind a shield deep enough to weather two dreadnoughts at once, and it carries its own strike wings to finish what the guns start. All that power points forward: its speed is glacial and its flanks and stern are thinly covered, so fast ships that reach the blind spot behind it can work unpunished where nothing swings to bear.

The CVS-class supercarrier is a mobile fortress-hangar, fielding nine wings of Covenant craft from behind a heavy shield. It mounts almost nothing for direct assault — a pair of heavy synergy batteries for long-range missile support and a dense skin of point-defense — and instead wages war entirely through its swarms of fighters and bombers. Immensely valuable and nearly defenseless up close, it must be screened at all costs; stripped of its escort, it is a slow, enormous prize.

The Seraph is the Covenant's frontline space-superiority craft, a heavy, well-armored fighter that fills two roles from the same airframe: a gun configuration that duels and escorts, and a bomber configuration that carries heavy ordnance against capital hulls. Sturdier than the strike craft it faces, it survives runs that would gut a lighter bomber, and its shielded pilots press attacks with a discipline that unnerves human squadrons.

The Type-26 Banshee is a light, fast attack craft thrown into battle in great numbers. Individually fragile and lightly armed, it relies on speed and sheer count, swarming larger ships to overwhelm their point defense and harry their flanks. Cheap to field and quick to replace, a cloud of Type-26s is less a squadron than a weather front.

The Type-27 Banshee is the heavier cousin of the Type-26, rebuilt as a dedicated interceptor. Faster and better armed than the swarm craft it flies alongside, it runs down enemy fighters and bombers before they reach the battle line, its long attack runs and elite handling making it the Covenant's answer to hostile air. Rarer and costlier than its little sibling, it is flown by the fleet's best.
